devpost_first_sections: Over 25% of our elderly population has difficult or is completely unable to do activities necessary for everyday life, like climbing up stairs. As you get older, your muscles weaken greatly to the point where, by your 80s, up to 50% of your muscle mass is gone. We developed Strider to bring back the mobility and independence that being able to walk comfortably provides to those who might normally struggle.

Strider uses IMUs to detect different stages of your gait cycle to determine when to apply motor aid. Using its two motors, it can alleviate up to 40 lbs of force in total. The level of assistance can be adjusted, even to negative values, to allow for "progressive overload" of walking, allowing users to become more comfortable walking without aid.

We type them again and again, often from documents we already have sitting in Google Drive or iCloud. Browser autofill only covers a handful of basic fields and stops at anything like an SSN, a driver's license number or a VIN. Businesses feel it too, because every extra minute on a long form is a chance for someone to give up. We wanted something like Stripe Checkout, but for forms: one button a business can drop in, that fills the whole form from the user's own data, while the user stays in control of exactly what gets shared.

A business adds a Fill with Formly button to its form. When you press it, a secure Formly window opens, and: You connect your data once. Formly builds your digital twin. It reads everything and keeps a private, organized profile of the facts forms ask for, each one linked back to the file it came from. devpost_first_sections: Seeing the growing number of cancer patients around the world and with two of our team members having multiple family members directly affected by the disease, we thought of making a bot that can preemptively help detect skin cancer at its early stages so that people can get the desired treatment. Annually, around 200,000 individuals globally are diagnosed with melanoma, and despite rapid advances in oncological treatment, many find out too late. This inspired us to design OncoBot as a way to help worried individuals check for skin cancer.

OncoBot allows patients to inspect suspicious marks on their skin and directs them to nearby medical services. Using computer vision, the program detects the presence of melanoma from the images that the user inputs. It utilizes various image processing techniques to remove noise from images and try to find potentially dangerous lesions. Additionally, the bot uses a Google Maps API to navigate the user to their nearest 5 hospitals for further examination if they type in an address.

devpost_first_sections: Between credit cards, memberships, and loyalty programs, we all collect benefits faster than we use them. Every store wants you to join its rewards program. Download the app. Make an account. Remember the password. Congratulations: you now have another coupon to forget about. VISA found that consumers hold an average of 17.4 loyalty memberships but actively use only 8.8. In fact, Americans miss out on up to $10 billion in loyalty savings every year ! People are signing up for rewards, earning benefits, and then forgetting they ever existed! So we built Lapse: a browser extension that remembers your rewards and does the checkout math for you, because we're obsessed with our customers.

It finds coupons, checks your coupons, memberships, and credit card benefits to find the best combination that gives our customers the best deal. We call this "stacking". Lapse also keeps track of what’s about to expire , so a reward you meant to “save for later” will be pushed to the front of the stack so you'll actually get a chance to use it before it's gone. From January 1 to April 13, 2025, the Florida Forest Service counted 1,300 wildfires and 57,025 acres burned ( FOX 35 ). Much of that land is remote: no power lines, no cell signal, nobody watching. Satellites can't close that gap on their own. The ones sharp enough to see a small fire pass over a few times a day: VIIRS has about 375 m pixels and 3 to 4 looks a day at mid-latitudes ( NASA Earthdata ). Ground cameras see smoke sooner, but they need a tower, grid power and an internet connection. We wanted a camera box you can strap to a tree in the middle of nowhere that decides on its own whether it is seeing smoke, and that sends only what matters.

Wild fires can rapidly spread, especially in certain environments, including water deprived areas. Insurance companies are decreasing coverage or discontinuing altogether due to the high disaster risk. Our goal for this project was to develop a product that is able to take measurements of temperature, soil moisture, and humidity in order to see trends and possibly predict and prepare for wild fires.

Our projects consists of two parts - a hard ware portion consisting of an Arduino board with multiple sensors connected to a Raspberry Pi, and a web application that tracks real time metrics from the sensors, with a robust LLM that uses our metrics to answer questions. The workflow is as follows: the Arduino board tracks metrics such as temperature, humidity, and soil moisture. This data is pushed to the Raspberry Pi, which uploads the data to a non-relational database. Our full-stack web application, which is built on Next.js and various UI frameworks, watches the database and updates the graphs and LLMs accordingly. ATP calls the insurer on behalf of a medical practice. The doctor joins the same live conversation , addresses the issue, and presses # to hand the call back. ATP then continues with the context from what the doctor and insurer discussed.
